questions.questionText: Which is a vector quantity?

options.text: density
mass
pressure
weight

questions.questionText:
The table shows the mass and volume of three different liquids, X, Y and Z.
liquid mass/g volume/cm3
X 120 200
Y 80 67
Z 100 120
The liquids are placed in the same container. The liquids do not mix.
Which liquid is at the top of the container and which liquid is at the bottom?
liquid at liquid at
top bottom

options.text: X Y
X Z
Y X
Y Z

questions.questionText: Which moving object has a resultant force acting on it?

options.text: a diver rising vertically through water at constant speed
an aircraft circling an airport at constant speed
a train going up a straight incline at constant speed
a parachutist descending vertically at terminal velocity

questions.questionText:
A sphere X collides head on with a second identical sphere Y which is stationary.
The mass of each sphere is 0.15kg.
Sphere X is travelling at a velocity of 2.0m/s before the collision and produces an impulse of
0.21Ns on sphere Y.
What is the velocity of sphere X after collision?

options.text: 0.60m/s in the opposite direction to Y
0.60m/s in the same direction as Y
1.4m/s in the opposite direction to Y
1.4m/s in the same direction as Y

questions.questionText:
A cyclist travels down a hill from rest at point X without pedalling.
The cyclist applies his brakes and the cycle stops at point Y.
hill
Which energy transfers have taken place between X and Y?

options.text: gravitational potential  kinetic  internal (thermal)
gravitational potential  internal (thermal)  kinetic
kinetic  gravitational potential  internal (thermal)
kinetic  internal (thermal)  gravitational potential

questions.questionText: Why can a gas be compressed easily into a smaller volume?

options.text: The particles are far apart.
The particles do not attract each other.
The particles move randomly.
The volume of each particle can be reduced.

questions.questionText:
A gas is contained in a cylinder by a movable piston.
gas
cylinder piston
The gas is heated so that it expands at constant pressure.
How is the force of each collision of a gas particle with the piston affected and how does the
frequency of collisions between the gas particles and the piston change?
force frequency

options.text: increases decreases
increases increases
stays the same decreases
stays the same increases

questions.questionText:
On a warm day, a carton of fresh milk is covered with a wet cloth.
Why does this help to reduce the temperature of the milk?

options.text: Some water evaporates from the cloth so the remaining water becomes cooler.
The water has a very high specific heat capacity.
The water insulates the milk from the warm air around it.
Water is always colder than the air around it.

questions.questionText:
The diagram shows the view of a room heated by a radiator. The arrowed line from X to Y is the
path of the convection current in the air.
ceiling
radiator
floor
Which row about the air temperature and the air density at X and at Y is correct?
air temperature air density

options.text: higher at X higher at X
higher at X higher at Y
higher at Y higher at Y
higher at Y higher at X

questions.questionText:
Two men, P and Q, stand close to a gap in a wall, as shown. Man P cannot see man Q but man
P can hear man Q speaking.
gap
Which statement explains this?

options.text: Light waves do not diffract at all because they are electromagnetic waves.
Light waves have a range of frequencies but sound has just one frequency.
Sound waves are of a higher frequency than light waves.
Sound waves diffract a lot because their wavelength is a similar size to the width of the gap.

questions.questionText: Which quantities relating to a wave on the surface of water can both be measured in metres?

options.text: amplitude and frequency
amplitude and wavelength
amplitude and wave speed
frequency and wavelength

questions.questionText:
A ray of light is reflected by a plane mirror.
Q R
P S
Which row shows the angle of incidence and the angle of reflection?
angle of angle of
incidence reflection

options.text: P Q
P S
Q R
R S

questions.questionText:
A thin converging lens is used to produce a real image of an object.
Which statement about the real image is always correct?

options.text: It is nearer to the lens than the object.
It is on the opposite side of the lens to the object.
It is the same size as the object.
It is upright.

questions.questionText:
The element mercury exists as a solid, a liquid or a gas.
Which row gives a possible set of values of the speeds of sound through mercury?
speed of sound in speed of sound in speed of sound in
frozen mercury liquid mercury mercury vapour
m / s m / s m / s

Which metal could be used for a permanent magnet and which metal could be used for the core
of an electromagnet?
permanent core of
magnet electromagnet

options.text: iron copper
iron steel
steel copper
steel iron

questions.questionText: Which statement describes the direction of an electric field at a point?

options.text: the direction of the force on a negative charge
the direction of the force on an N pole
the direction of the force on a positive charge
the direction of the force on an S pole

questions.questionText: Which statement about a voltmeter is correct?

options.text: It has a scale which is marked in amperes (A).
It must be connected in series in a circuit.
It measures potential difference (p.d.).
It must have three terminals.

questions.questionText:
A plastic rod is rubbed with a cloth. The rod becomes positively charged because of the
movement of charged particles.
Which row gives the name of these charged particles and the direction in which they move?
charged direction of
particles movement

options.text: electrons from cloth to rod
electrons from rod to cloth
protons from cloth to rod
protons from rod to cloth

questions.questionText:
A current in a solenoid produces a uniform magnetic field inside the solenoid. The magnetic field
direction is due east.
Which changes will produce a stronger magnetic field with a direction due west?

options.text: Use a smaller current and turn the solenoid through 180.
Use a smaller current and reverse the current.
Use a larger current and turn the solenoid through 90.
Use a larger current and reverse the current.

questions.questionText:
A metal rod PQ rests on two horizontal metal wires that are attached to a battery. The rod lies
between the poles of a magnet.
magnet
metal rod
magnet
When the switch is closed, the rod moves to the right.
What could be changed so that the rod moves to the left?

options.text: Open the switch.
Reverse the battery terminals and exchange the poles of the magnet.
Reverse the battery terminals but without exchanging the poles of the magnet.
Turn the metal rod around (P and Q exchanged).

questions.questionText:
A transformer in a computer is used to transform the mains voltage of 240V to 12V.
The number of turns on the secondary coil is 2000.
Which statement about the transformer is correct?

options.text: It is a step-down transformer and has 100 turns on its primary coil.
It is a step-down transformer and has 40000 turns on its primary coil.
It is a step-up transformer and has 100 turns on its primary coil.
It is a step-up transformer and has 40000 turns on its primary coil.

questions.questionText:
In -particle scattering, -particles are incident on a thin metal foil.
Which row describes results from the experiment and a conclusion that the results lead to?
results conclusion

options.text: most of the -particles most of the atom is empty space pass straight through the foil
most of the -particles the nucleus is very large pass straight through the foil
very few of the -particles most of the atom is empty space pass straight through the foil
very few of the -particles the nucleus is very large pass straight through the foil

questions.questionText:
-particles, -particles and -rays are emitted by radioactive nuclei when they decay.
Which emissions can be deflected by an electric field?

options.text: -particles, -particles and -rays
-particles and -particles only
-particles and -rays only
-rays and -particles only

questions.questionText: Which particle is absorbed by a nucleus to cause nuclear fission?

options.text: a neutron
a proton
an -particle
a -particle

questions.questionText:
It is summer in the northern hemisphere of the Earth in June.
Which statement explains why?

options.text: The Earth is closer to the Sun in June.
The Earth spins on its axis in the opposite direction to that in which it rotates around the Sun.
The Moon is full in June.
The north pole of the axis of the Earth’s rotation is tilted towards the Sun in June.

questions.questionText: Which statement about the Sun is correct?

options.text: The Sun is a dwarf star consisting mostly of hydrogen and oxygen.
The Sun is a giant star consisting mostly of helium and carbon dioxide.
The Sun is a medium-sized star consisting mostly of hydrogen and helium.
The Sun is a medium-sized star consisting mostly of nitrogen and oxygen.
